cards.text: Two kingdoms now: Israel and Judah. Jehoash son of Jehoahaz is in his second year as king of Israel when Amaziah son of Joash becomes king of Judah. Amaziah is twenty-five, and he'll reign in Jerusalem twenty-nine years.

cards.question: True or false: Amaziah, the new king of Judah, does what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Right, but with a catch: not as his father David had done. Good, not great, like a cookie that's baked all the way but still a little pale.

cards.question: Amaziah doesn't do things the way David did. Instead, he does everything as which father had done?

cards.text: Nevertheless, one spot gets missed: the high places are not taken away. That's like cleaning the whole kitchen and stuffing the mess in a drawer, and believe me, friend, I KNOW what goes on in drawers.

cards.question: The high places are still standing in Amaziah's day. What do the people keep doing there?

cards.text: As soon as the kingdom is firmly in his grasp, Amaziah turns to some old business. Some of the servants had murdered his father, King Joash.

cards.question: What does Amaziah do to the servants who murdered his father?

cards.text: But here's the twist. Those murderers had sons, and Amaziah goes by what's written in the Book of the Law of Moses.

cards.question: So what happens to the sons of the men who murdered Amaziah's father?

answers.text: They are not put to death
They are put to death too
They are sent out of Judah

cards.question: The LORD's command in the Law of Moses says, "Fathers must not be put to death for their ___, and children must not be put to death for their ___; each is to die for his own sin."

cards.text: Then Amaziah goes to war against the Edomites, in a place called the Valley of Salt.

cards.question: How many Edomites does Amaziah strike down in the Valley of Salt?
Amaziah also takes the city of Sela in battle. What does he do with it?

answers.text: He gives it a new name

cards.text: He calls it Joktheel, and that's its name to this very day. The last thing I ever renamed was a burnt cookie, and I called it EXTRA CRUNCHY.
Two big wins, and now Amaziah is looking north. He sends messengers to Jehoash king of Israel.

cards.question: What message does Amaziah, king of Judah, send to Jehoash king of Israel?

answers.text: Come and meet me face to face
Send me gold for my temple

cards.text: Jehoash king of Israel answers Amaziah with a little story. It starts in Lebanon, with a thistle and a cedar.

cards.question: In Jehoash's story, a thistle in Lebanon sends a message to a cedar in Lebanon. What does the thistle ask for?

answers.text: The cedar's daughter for its son
A place in the cedar's shade

cards.text: A THISTLE. Asking a CEDAR to join the family? That's me rolling into a five-star kitchen and asking the head chef for his daughter's hand.

cards.question: Then something else in Lebanon comes along. What happens to the thistle in Jehoash's story?

cards.text: Then Jehoash drops the story and talks straight to Amaziah. Yes, he says, you have indeed defeated Edom.

cards.question: Jehoash tells Amaziah that after beating Edom, his heart has become ___.
So what does Jehoash tell Amaziah to do?

answers.text: Enjoy the win and stay home

cards.question: True or false: Jehoash warns Amaziah that if he stirs up trouble, he could fall and take Judah with him.

cards.text: Translation: congratulations on Edom, now go frame the trophy. Take the win. Stay. HOME.

cards.question: True or false: Amaziah listens to Jehoash's warning and stays home.

cards.text: Amaziah would not listen, so Jehoash king of Israel advances. The two kings face each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

cards.question: Judah and Israel clash at Beth-shemesh. How does the battle go for Judah?

answers.text: Judah is routed and runs home
The battle ends in a truce

cards.text: Every man flees to his home. Which is funny, because home is exactly where Jehoash told Amaziah to stay in the first place.

cards.question: What happens to Amaziah himself at Beth-shemesh?

cards.text: With Amaziah captured, Jehoash goes to Jerusalem. He breaks down four hundred cubits of the wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.

cards.question: Jehoash takes all the gold and silver and articles he finds in Jerusalem. Where does he find them?

answers.text: The house of the LORD and the palace
The houses of the city's elders
The storerooms by the city gates

cards.question: True or false: Jehoash also takes some hostages and returns to Samaria.

cards.text: The rest of Jehoash's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. He rests with his fathers, is buried in Samaria, and his son Jeroboam reigns in his place.

cards.question: True or false: Amaziah king of Judah outlives Jehoash king of Israel.

cards.text: He does, by fifteen years. Fifteen whole years to think about that thistle story.
The rest of Amaziah's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Then conspirators in Jerusalem plot against him, and he flees.

cards.question: Conspirators plot against Amaziah in Jerusalem. Where does he flee?
True or false: Once Amaziah reaches Lachish, he's safe from the conspirators.

cards.text: Men are sent after him, and they kill him there in Lachish. He's carried back on horses and buried with his fathers in Jerusalem, in the City of David.

cards.question: Who do the people of Judah make king in place of Amaziah?
Azariah, the new king of Judah, is only ___ years old.

cards.text: Sixteen years old, with a whole kingdom on his shoulders. And Azariah is the one who rebuilds Elath and restores it to Judah after Amaziah rests with his fathers.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "Fathers must not be put to death for their ___, and children must not be put to death for their ___; each is to die for his own sin.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: David first appears here as "his father David" with nothing saying who he is. One card later, card 4 asks which "father" Amaziah followed, Joash. A baker can easily think David was Amaziah's actual father, since card 1 already said Amaziah is the son of Joash. Say simply who David is, for example his ancestor King David.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "One spot gets missed" tells the baker the high places stayed because of an oversight. The joke about "cleaning the whole kitchen" also implies Amaziah cleared everything else away. 2 Kings 14:4 only says the high places were not taken away. It gives no reason and says nothing about anything else being removed.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The setup line "But here's the twist" signals that Amaziah spares the sons. That rules out the wrong answer "They are put to death too" on card 10 before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The Edomites appear for the first time and nothing says who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says, in his own voice and without quotation marks, "that's its name to this very day." In 2 Kings 14:7, "to this very day" means the writer's day. Said as his own present-tense statement, it can sound like a claim that the place is still called Joktheel today.
findings.question: When Papa Dorin paraphrases phrases like "to this very day," should he quote them exactly or say they're the writer's words, so they don't read as a claim about today?

findings.problem: In the parable, the thistle asks for the cedar's daughter as a wife for its son. In the joke, Papa Dorin asks for the head chef's daughter's hand himself, so the action doesn't match. It also puts Papa Dorin in a marriage scenario, though his family is only his six kids and there is no wife.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This card only restates what card 7 already taught, that Amaziah should enjoy the win and stay home. It tells nothing new from the passage.
"Which is funny, because home is exactly where..." explains the joke instead of letting the callback land. The card also mostly repeats card 3's right answer, "Judah is routed and runs home."
This story card carries three things: the rest of Jehoash's acts being written in the Chronicles, his death and burial in Samaria, and Jeroboam reigning in his place.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The word "only" in "is only ___ years old" rules out "thirty." That leaves a coin flip between sixteen and twelve.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Stop 3 has almost no real humor. Its only attempts are a joke that gets explained (card 4) and a mild line (card 11). The rest reads as plain narration through moments that could hold a laugh without muddying a fact, like Judah's army fleeing home and Amaziah being captured.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
